#42242 has hit a case where the a norm_num proof works without the module system, but fails under it.
This works

import Mathlib.NumberTheory.LucasLehmer
example : ¬ LucasLehmerTest 2 := by norm_num

but this fails

module
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.LucasLehmer
example : ¬ LucasLehmerTest 2 := by norm_num

Perhaps this is me not understanding the meta phase well enough yet: the relevant norm_num extension is defined in evalLucasLehmerTest which is a public meta def.
meta defs are not exposed by default so smodNatTR requires an explicit @[expose] annotation

I'm confused. Why are we using sModNatTR inside of the proof terms? I would expect from the docstring of sModNat ("This can be reduced by the kernel.") that it would be used instead, and that sModNatTR is just to make the compiled code tail recursive.
Hmm, you're right this is a bit weird with the comments; it would probably be better to use sModNat in the proof terms and sModNatTR in meta code
